title: Security, monitoring and cost
content:
1. Review permissions and secrets Go to IAM → Roles and inspect the execution roles and task roles created by the stacks. Verify that ECR repositories, S3 buckets, Secrets Manager, and ECS tasks are granted permissions appropriate for your environment. Do not capture policies containing your account ID without redacting it. The EC2 builder should only exist while building images.
Roles and policy scope for the lab environment; redact account identifiers. RDS, Valkey, and the services run in private subnets; secrets are referenced by ARN. CloudFront uses WAF and a VPC origin pointing to an internal ALB. The current configuration is intended for lab use—review internal transport encryption, backups, IAM policies, and WAF rules before serving real users.
2. Inspect CloudWatch Logs, Metrics, and Alarms In ECS → Clusters → service → Tasks → task → Logs, or CloudWatch → Log groups, review logs during task startup and while running a test meeting (tina-full.yml automatically provisions 13 Log Groups for all ECS services and enables CloudWatchMetricsEnabled on AWS WAF). In CloudFormation, the Events tab shows stack provisioning errors. Do not include access tokens, meeting URLs, transcript content, or personal data in screenshots.
CloudWatch task logs with tokens, user details, and meeting content redacted. To monitor system health, open CloudWatch → Metrics → All metrics and check AWS/ECS (CPUUtilization, MemoryUtilization), AWS/ApplicationELB (HTTPCode_Target_5XX_Count, HealthyHostCount), and AWS/RDS (CPUUtilization, FreeStorageSpace, DatabaseConnections). When you need full operational alerting (10 Metric Filters, 20 Alarms, and a unified Dashboard), deploy deploy/aws/staging-workspace-s3-monitoring.yml from main (see Section 5.4.3.5 ).
If ECS reports CannotPullContainerError, check that the digest is ARM64, the execution role has ECR permissions, and outbound NAT routing works. If you hit quota limits, check Service Quotas. If targets are unhealthy, inspect Terminal logs, port 3000, and the /api/auth/providers health check path.
3. Cost Estimation and Optimization Check Billing → Budgets and Cost Explorer; billing data can lag behind actual usage. Budgets send alerts only—they do not automatically delete resources.
Reference Cost Estimate (us-east-1, single pilot environment) The table below uses official AWS us-east-1 on-demand pricing (730 h/month) for a single pilot environment (≈10 users, ≈5 meetings/week, ≈20 meeting-hours/month):
Service Category Key Sizing Est. Monthly Cost ECS Fargate (ARM64) Web/Agent 24/7 (≈$28.80) + Bot/VieGem/VieNeu on-demand ≈20 h/month (≈$3.20) ≈$32.00 Networking 1 Internal ALB (≈$18.00) + 1 NAT Gateway (≈$33.30) + 1 Public IPv4 for NAT (≈$3.65) + CloudFront (≈$1.00) ≈$55.95 Data Stores RDS PostgreSQL db.t4g.micro + 20 GB gp3 (≈$14.00) + ElastiCache Valkey cache.t4g.micro (≈$9.34) + S3 (≈$0.33) ≈$23.67 AI & Messaging Amazon Bedrock amazon.nova-lite-v1:0 (≈$0.54; budgeted with fallback ≈$3.00) + optional Amazon SES (≈$0.01) ≈$3.01 Security & Observability AWS WAF (≈$8.00) + Secrets Manager (≈$2.00) + KMS (≈$1.00) + CloudWatch (≈$3.50) + ECR (≈$1.00) ≈$15.50 Total (24/7 full stack) Full single pilot environment ≈$130.13/month Hands-on lab session (2–3 h) Deploy, validate, and delete per Section 5.6 ≈$1–2 / lab session Note: If you deploy the combined tina-full.yml template (5.4A) and leave all optional services (Voice, Agent, MCP, Flows, and 4 VPC Interface Endpoints) running 24/7 without deleting them, monthly costs will be higher than the lean table above. Always run cleanup in Section 5.6 right after finishing the lab.
Cost Optimization Strategies ARM64 (Graviton) on Fargate & RDS t4g: reduces compute costs by ≈20% compared to equivalent x86_64 sizing. VPC Endpoints (free S3 Gateway + ECR/Logs/Secrets Manager): keeps private image pulls, logs, and secret reads off the NAT Gateway, avoiding $0.045/GB NAT data processing fees. Off-hours scale-down: scaling non-essential ECS services to desiredCount=0 and stopping RDS outside working hours (≈10 h/day, weekdays) lowers pilot costs to ≈$70–80/month. On-demand Bot & meeting tasks: Bot tasks are spawned only when a meeting starts and stop automatically when it ends, avoiding 24/7 idle compute. S3 Lifecycle & AWS Budgets: auto-expire temporary runtime-invocations/ objects after 1 day, transition older recordings to cheaper storage classes, and set AWS Budgets alerts at 50%, 80%, and 100%. Lab account budget and alert status; redact email addresses and account ID. When you finish the lab, proceed to cleanup to avoid ongoing charges.

title: Workshop
content:

This walkthrough combines the AWS Console for CloudFormation, EC2, and WAF with the AWS CLI and CloudFormation for the remaining steps. You do not need access to the author’s account or machine.

This workshop deploys a single-AZ data layer to keep lab costs low and is intended for lab/pilot evaluation rather than High Availability production.
The initial deployment runs Terminal in meetings mode, Google sign-in, the meeting bot, and optionally VieGem for non-commercial transcription testing. Full workspace/agent capabilities, voice assistant, additional models, and extra integrations are not enabled by default in this build; see the extensions section .
Quick Single-File Deployment (Recommended) See single CloudFormation deployment to use the combined tina-full.yml template together with the pre-built set of 15 ARM64 images on GHCR (including VieGem and 3 Voice images): simply paste 5 short commands into AWS CloudShell (~15–20 minutes), then attach your own Google OAuth credentials to run the full web app. The multi-stack walkthrough below is for cases where you want to build and inspect each infrastructure layer individually.
Walkthrough Order Overview and acceptance criteria . Account, quotas, and source code preparation . VPC and network foundation . Build images, create data stores, deploy the website, and test . Monitoring and costs . Cleanup and evidence . Estimated completion time is 15–20 minutes using the quick single-stack path in 5.4A (copying prebuilt images from GHCR), or 30–45 minutes for the multi-stack path (depending on RDS, ElastiCache, and CloudFront provisioning times). AWS resources and data transfer may incur charges as soon as resources are created; remember to clean up all resources in Section 5.6 when finished.
Guide Screenshots Each step in this workshop includes real screenshots from the AWS Console and the deployed TINA web application directly beneath the corresponding instructions so you can easily verify your progress. title: Cleanup and evidence
content:
1. Confirm resources belong to the workshop The deletion commands below remove your lab environment and test data. Proceed only after saving anything you need to keep and verifying the account, Region, and stack names. Do not delete resources belonging to other environments. Before deleting stacks, end any active meetings, wait for bot tasks to stop, and terminate the EC2 builder created during the lab.
2. Delete stacks in reverse dependency order In CloudShell, delete each stack and wait for it to finish before deleting the next. Omit tina-ws-viegem if you did not deploy it:
for s in tina-ws-terminal tina-ws-core tina-ws-viegem tina-ws-runtime tina-ws-bot tina-ws-edge tina-ws-data tina-ws-egress; do aws cloudformation delete-stack --region "$AWS_REGION" --stack-name "$s" aws cloudformation wait stack-delete-complete --region "$AWS_REGION" --stack-name "$s" done If an error occurs, stop and read CloudFormation → Events to resolve the dependency instead of continuing blindly. CloudFront distributions can take time to delete. Do not delete the foundation stack yet if repositories managed by it still contain images: ECR can reject deleting non-empty repositories.
3. Review ECR, buckets, snapshots, and roles ECR: For the three repositories tina-staging/bot, tina-staging/runtime, and tina-staging/meeting-api, select all lab images and click Delete. Then delete the foundation stack:
aws cloudformation delete-stack --region "$AWS_REGION" --stack-name tina-staging aws cloudformation wait stack-delete-complete --region "$AWS_REGION" --stack-name tina-staging The remaining four ECR repositories were created manually via CLI, so they are not deleted automatically; in the Console, select tina-staging/terminal, gateway, admin-api, and viegem and delete them once you are sure you no longer need the images.
S3: The foundation stack uses DeletionPolicy: Retain, so the recordings bucket and its objects remain. In S3, identify the exact bucket from your saved outputs, download anything you want to keep, and then choose Empty → Delete if you want to remove all test data. Never delete a bucket solely because its name looks similar.
RDS → Snapshots: The data stack retains a final snapshot when deleting the database. Keep it if you need to restore later, or delete the test snapshot after reviewing it. Retained snapshots and buckets can continue to incur charges.
WAF: Delete the tina-workshop-acl Web ACL after the edge stack is removed. Secrets Manager: The manually created Google secret remains; delete it according to your policy if no longer needed. Optionally delete remaining log groups once you no longer need evidence.
After the builder instance is terminated, remove the role from its instance profile and delete the exact IAM resources created for the lab. For example:
aws iam remove-role-from-instance-profile --instance-profile-name tina-workshop-builder-profile --role-name tina-workshop-builder-role aws iam delete-instance-profile --instance-profile-name tina-workshop-builder-profile aws iam delete-role-policy --role-name tina-workshop-builder-role --policy-name TinaEcrPush aws iam detach-role-policy --role-name tina-workshop-builder-role --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore aws iam delete-role --role-name tina-workshop-builder-role Re-check EC2/EBS, NAT/EIP, ECS, RDS, ElastiCache, CloudFront, WAF, S3, ECR, and Billing to confirm no unintended test resources remain.
Resource cleanup status of the lab environment after verification; redact the account ID. 4. Evidence for evaluation Record the date, commit 8a2b79e884bc0833f9075d4e795b20d347cef9c2, the status of each step, any errors encountered, and how they were resolved. Screenshots must be genuine captures placed at their corresponding steps; do not include secrets, real transcripts, or personal information in public documentation.
